name: Azure DocumentDB
aliases: vCore-based Azure Cosmos DB for MongoDB
tagline: Microsoft's managed MongoDB-compatible service, built on the open-source DocumentDB engine.
description: Azure DocumentDB is Microsoft's managed, vCore-priced, MongoDB-compatible document database. It was previously sold as vCore-based Azure Cosmos DB for MongoDB and was renamed at general availability on 18 November 2025. It runs the MIT-licensed DocumentDB engine (PostgreSQL plus BSON extensions), not MongoDB code, and claims about 99% MongoDB API compatibility. It includes integrated vector search, a free tier and automatic sharding once data grows large. Microsoft positions it for scale-up workloads with rich aggregation, and keeps Cosmos DB for globally distributed scale-out work, so the choice between the two matters.

license.name: Proprietary Azure service (engine is MIT-licensed DocumentDB)

pricing.notes: Compute (vCores) and storage billed independently; backups included. A free tier includes vector search.

scale.notes: Vertical scaling first; shards automatically (no shard key needed until multi-TB). Cross-region geo-replicas for DR.

strengths: Predictable vCore pricing instead of request units
Engine is open source, so you can run the same thing locally or on another cloud
Integrated vector search, including on the free tier
Strong aggregation-pipeline and multi-document transaction fidelity
Entra ID, Azure Monitor and Private Link integration
weaknesses: 99.995% SLA and regional deployment, below Cosmos DB's multi-region 99.999%
Compatibility is high but not complete; test edge-case operators
Naming history (Cosmos DB for MongoDB vCore vs RU) causes confusion in docs and tooling
useCases: MongoDB migrations to Azure without SSPL
Content management and catalog backends with complex aggregations
RAG applications storing embeddings next to documents
notIdealFor: Globally distributed multi-region writes (use Cosmos DB)
Apps that need features exclusive to MongoDB Atlas
